messages:
sam: Quick sanity check — running an isolation test for prefetch thresholds on q4_13b. Goal: measure where prefetch helps latency without increasing top-1 hallucinations for our longform set. Planning a micro-grid over thresholds [0.2,0.4,0.6,0.8] with deterministic sampling.

marta.g: Sounds good. Can you share the exact job command so infra can mirror it? Include flags for logging KV hits and saving first-256 token traces.

sam: Yep, pasted the exact launcher we used:

```
python bench.py \
  --model redwood-llama-13b-q4 \
  --prefetch true \
  --prefetch-threshold 0.6 \
  --speculative false \
  --sampling top_k=40,top_p=0.95 \
  --deterministic \
  --batch 4 \
  --eval-set longform_2k.json \
  --save-traces 256 \
  --log-prefix pf-thresh-1784209
```

nyla: For comparability please run the same grid but with `--quant-mode q8` and `--q4` (two separate runs) — we want to see whether quant noise interacts with prefetch heuristics. Also add `--save-logits 200` for entropy analysis.

dave_ops: I can spin up the four runs. ETA: ~3h to complete grid for one quant mode. Ops-bot: reserve 8 GPUs on cluster-ml-west for 4h.

ops-bot: Resources reserved: 8 gpus on cluster-ml-west, jobs queued: bench/1784209-{0..3}. Estimated start in 12m.

sam: Quick abort criteria — if p95 > baseline p95 * 1.25 or halluc_rate increases by >1.0% absolute, cancel the rest. Also abort if kv_fill_time spikes >2x.

marta.g: Good. Capture these metrics in per-job metadata: p50/p95/p99 latency, kv_fill_time_ms, kv_hit_rate, halluc_rate_abs, BLEU, exact_match. Tag outputs with `pf_thresh_{t}`.

(3h later)

ops-bot: Jobs completed: bench/1784209-0..3. Artifacts uploaded to gs://redwood-expts/pf-thresh/1784209/.

sam: Quick top-level numbers (longform_2k):
- baseline (no-prefetch): p50 92ms, p95 240ms, halluc 3.9%
- pf 0.2: p50 90ms, p95 228ms, halluc 4.0%
- pf 0.4: p50 86ms, p95 215ms, halluc 4.1%
- pf 0.6: p50 79ms, p95 188ms, halluc 5.4% <-- red flag
- pf 0.8: p50 75ms, p95 170ms, halluc 7.1% <-- big regression
- kv_hit_rate increases monotonically with threshold (baseline 1.9% -> 0.2:2.5% -> 0.4:3.6% -> 0.6:5.1% -> 0.8:6.9%)

nyla: Interesting — entropy traces show a small downward shift in early tokens for higher thresholds, but divergence starts around token 120 where prefetch-augmented contexts seem to bias sampling toward higher-prob tokens, paradoxically increasing hallucination downstream. I'll upload the per-token KL plots.

dave_ops: Re-ran a sanity check with q8 mode for pf=0.6: p50 80ms, p95 195ms, halluc 4.3% (so quantization mode interacts a lot).

marta.g: So preliminary takeaway: prefetch threshold <=0.4 gives modest latency win without material quality hit. Past ~0.6 we see latency gains but a substantial hallucation jump on q4. Could be quant-induced sensitivity to slightly shifted context.

sam: Action items: 1) run 10k quality sweep for pf=0.4 and pf=0.6 in both q4 and q8 with deterministic seeds to tighten CIs; 2) dump raw logits for 500 examples around the divergence zone (tokens 100-180); 3) try a hybrid policy: prefetch only when kv_hit_prob > 0.5 AND prefix_length > 64.

nyla: I'll start the 10k sweep for pf=0.4/q4 and pf=0.6/q4 with `--save-outputs` + bootstrap CI notebook. Expect ~7-9h.

sam: Also add a run where we keep speculative on but set prefetch-threshold 0.6 — we want to see if speculation mitigates the halluc spike (hypothesis: speculation can mask prefetch timing shifts).

dave_ops: Queued. ops-bot: bench/1784210 (speculative+pf0.6) queued on cluster-ml-west.

ops-bot: Job queued: bench/1784210 -> expected start 20m.

marta.g: Great. For the spec doc: include the minimal grid, a visualization of kv_hit_rate vs halluc_rate, and a short note about quant-sensitivity. We'll likely recommend defaulting to pf=0.4 for q4 models until we solve the drift.

sam: One last ask — include a tiny A/B on a few safety-sensitive prompts (3 examples) to check if hallucination patterns are semantically dangerous, not just numeric.

nyla: On it. Uploading initial plots now. Will post final summary when the 10k sweeps finish.
